evidence.title: Proactive care management of AI-identified at-risk patients decreases preventable admissions
evidence.venue: The American journal of managed care
evidence.outcome: Preventable admissions after proactive care management outreach to AI-identified high-risk patients
evidence.effect: Care management for AI-identified at-risk patients was followed by a 27% significant drop in potentially preventable hospital admissions (95% CI -44% to -6%).
evidence.quote: A care management intervention targeting AI-identified at-risk patients was followed by a onetime, significant, sizable reduction in preventable HA rates.

evidence.title: Comparing clinical decision support systems for improving follow-up of abnormal cervical cancer screening test results
evidence.effect: CDSS with patient outreach increased follow-up to 38.2% vs 23.5% in System A, and 25.4% vs 19.7% in System B, whereas CDSS alone did not.
evidence.quote: CDSS with patient outreach with or without navigation versus usual care significantly increased follow-up rates in System A (38.2 % or 37.2 % vs 23.5 %, p < 0.001) and System B (25.4 % or 23 % vs. 19.7 %, p = 0.044).

evidence.title: Connecting Risk Prediction to Intervention: Evidence from a Randomized Trial Testing Patient Navigation and Education to Improve Postpartum Outcomes
evidence.venue: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
evidence.outcome: 30-day postpartum hospital use after navigation and education for patients flagged high-risk by the calculator
evidence.effect: Hospital use was 20.0% in the intervention group vs 16.4% in controls (RR 1.2, 95% CI 0.7-2.0). Estimates did not suggest reduced hospital use. Secondary outcomes were similar between groups.
evidence.quote: Incidence was 20.0% among intervention participants and 16.4% among control participants (risk ratio [95% confidence interval] = 1.2 [0.7-2.0]).

evidence.title: Implementation of risk prediction models using electronic health data for early detection of pancreatic cancer: a prospective pilot feasibility study
evidence.outcome: Enrollment and completion of imaging and CA19-9 workup among patients flagged high-risk by prediction models
evidence.effect: Of 1,251 eligible high-risk patients, 102 (8.2%) enrolled; 87% completed baseline imaging, 96% completed CA19-9; 79% completed both at 18 months; 10% needed further evaluations.
evidence.quote: At baseline, 89 (87%) completed imaging and 98 (96%) completed CA19-9.

evidence.title: Orlando Veterans Affairs Stratification Tool for Opioid Risk Mitigation (STORM) very high risk interdisciplinary team review: A brief report
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
evidence.outcome: Change in opioid dose, SUD treatment, and risk mitigation after interdisciplinary review of very high-risk patients
evidence.effect: Mean MEDD fell from 82.2 mg to 7.5 mg (90.9% reduction); medications for SUD rose in 3 patients (23%); SUD engagement rose from 3 to 6 patients; urine drug tests up 79%; benzodiazepine use down 50%. No comparator group.
evidence.quote: A reduction in MEDD, increase in SUD treatment, and improved risk mitigation was observed.

evidence.title: Implementation of a machine learning model and direct-to-patient outreach program for targeted screening for familial hypercholesterolemia
evidence.outcome: Clinical visits and new diagnoses yielded by direct-to-patient outreach to model-flagged high-risk patients
evidence.effect: Outreach yielded 72 clinical visits (19%) and 58 new diagnoses of possible/probable/definite FH (15%), versus about 0.4% expected in general-population screening. The process was labor intensive.
evidence.quote: A high-touch, direct-to-patient outreach process yielded 72 clinical visits (19%) and 58 new diagnoses of possible/probable/definite FH (15%).
evidence.sample_unit: patients flagged by the machine learning model

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Algorithms Improve Care of Patients with AAA
evidence.outcome: Long-term follow-up and scheduled monitoring for AI-detected AAA patients
evidence.effect: Long-term follow-up 45% vs. 30% (P = 0.004); scheduled monitoring appointments 99% vs. 65% (P < 0.001)
evidence.quote: A greater proportion of patients in the post-AI protocol group had long-term follow-up (45% vs. 30%, P = 0.004) and had scheduled appointments for long-term AAA monitoring (99% vs. 65%, P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Utilizing an Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Model to Predict Colorectal Cancer Risk in American Samoa: A Pilot Study
evidence.venue: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
evidence.outcome: Follow-up screening uptake among patients flagged high-risk by the model after outreach
evidence.effect: 62 high-risk participants identified and contacted; only 4 returned for further testing and 1 agreed to colonoscopy, limiting model validation.
evidence.quote: However, only four participants returned for further testing, and just one agreed to a colonoscopy.

evidence.title: Design and Preliminary Testing of the CardioCare System in Health Checkup Centers: Implementation Report
evidence.outcome: Attendance at follow-up clinic among high-risk individuals invited after risk flagging
evidence.effect: 181 of 2069 invited high-risk individuals (8.7%) attended at least 1 in-person visit; engaged patients gave positive feedback, but low uptake indicated significant barriers.
evidence.quote: However, patient engagement was low: of the 2069 high-risk individuals invited for follow-up care, 181 (8.7%) attended at least 1 in-person visit at the clinic.
evidence.sample_unit: high-risk older adults invited for follow-up

evidence.title: Improving follow-up of incidental pulmonary nodules in the emergency department using an artificial intelligence-supported workflow
evidence.outcome: Patient notification and nodule-specific follow-up before vs after AI-supported outreach workflow
evidence.effect: Notification rose from 171/228 (75%) to 223/252 (88.4%), p = 0.0001; nodule-specific follow-up rose from 122/228 (53.5%) to 171/252 (67.9%), p = 0.0012.
evidence.quote: With implementation of the AI-supported workflow, patient notification increased from 171/228 (75%) to 223/252 (88.4%) p = 0.0001, and nodule-specific follow-up increased from 122/228 (53.5%) to 171/252 (67.9%) p = 0.0012.
evidence.sample_unit: ED patients undergoing chest CT (228 pre, 252 post)

evidence.title: Effectiveness of an Emergency Department-Based Machine Learning Clinical Decision Support Tool to Prevent Outpatient Falls Among Older Adults: Protocol for a Quasi-Experimental Study
evidence.outcome: Appointment scheduling among high-risk patients referred to the mobility and falls clinic
evidence.effect: Only 15% (45/339) of referred patients had scheduled an appointment, documenting a downstream follow-up gap despite AI-based identification and referral.
evidence.quote: To date, 15% (45/339) of patients have scheduled an appointment with the clinic.

evidence.title: Real-world integration of an autonomous artificial intelligence system for diabetic retinopathy screening in an endocrinology outpatient clinic
evidence.outcome: Completion of confirmatory examination among AI-positive patients
evidence.effect: Of 76 AI-positive patients, 34 (44.7%) completed confirmatory examination at the institution's retina clinic; externally completed follow-up was not captured.
evidence.quote: Seventy-six (29.6%) patients screened positive for mtmDR, of whom 34 (44.7%) completed confirmatory examination at the institution's retina clinic; externally completed follow-up was not captured.

evidence.title: Evaluation of the Efficacy of Artificial Intelligence-Based Screening for Diabetic Retinopathy in a Predominantly Non-White Population
evidence.outcome: Follow-up attendance among patients with positive AI screen results
evidence.effect: 29.8% of patients with positive screen results did not attend their scheduled ophthalmology visit.
evidence.quote: It was found, however, that although most patients with a positive screen had ophthalmology referrals placed, 29.8% of patients with positive screen results did not attend their scheduled ophthalmology visit.

commentary.bottom_line: Two cluster randomized trials suggest that human outreach after AI risk flagging may raise follow-up completion and reduce preventable admissions, but a trial in a low-income population found no benefit and several descriptive studies report low uptake. No study tests care coordination for patients who lack the data needed for risk categorization.

perspectives.view: Three randomized trials test outreach after flagging. Two cluster trials favored outreach: a 27% drop in preventable admissions (95% CI -44% to -6%), and follow-up of 38.2% vs 23.5% and 25.4% vs 19.7%. A 220-patient trial found hospital use of 20.0% vs 16.4% (RR 1.2). Inconsistency and the untested coordination component lower certainty.

Hazard studies show that flagged patients often go unseen. Only 15% of referred patients scheduled a falls visit, 44.7% completed a confirmatory eye exam, and 29.8% missed an ophthalmology visit. Uncontrolled studies suggest that outreach workflows may close part of this gap, with nodule follow-up rising from 53.5% to 67.9% and scheduled aneurysm monitoring reaching 99% vs 65%.

In one cluster trial, decision support alone did not raise follow-up, while decision support paired with patient outreach did. This suggests that a risk flag may need a human contact step to change care. Direct outreach for familial hypercholesterolemia yielded 19% visits and 15% new diagnoses, and the authors described the process as labor intensive.

Uptake after outreach was low in several deployments. In one study, 8.2% of eligible high-risk patients enrolled in workup, 8.7% of invited older adults attended a follow-up clinic, and 4 of 62 contacted patients returned for testing. None of these studies reported staffing hours or cost per patient reached.

The only randomized trial focused on low-income and racial or ethnic minority patients found no reduction in postpartum hospital use after navigation and education. In American Samoa, 1 of 62 contacted high-risk patients agreed to colonoscopy. These results suggest that outreach alone may not overcome access barriers in these groups.

Outreach gives flagged patients a human contact. Patients who engaged with a follow-up clinic gave positive feedback, but 91.3% of invited patients did not attend. An interdisciplinary review of 13 very high-risk opioid patients was followed by more treatment engagement, from 3 to 6 patients. That study had no comparator group.

commentary.research_gap: No study tests how to identify or coordinate care for patients whose records lack the data needed for risk categorization. Trials comparing outreach intensities, reporting staffing cost, and measuring diagnostic and health outcomes by subgroup are also absent.
commentary.underserved_note: One trial enrolled low-income and racial or ethnic minority patients and found no benefit, and one descriptive study in American Samoa found very low return rates. The only safety-net population appears in a hazard study. No test enrolled Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy groups as defined populations, so the benefit seen in the two positive trials may not carry over to these patients.
